questions.q: What does Health Cloud's data model center on, instead of generic Accounts and Contacts?
options: Financial Holdings and Assets
Cases and Entitlements
Patients and Households
Opportunities and Products
questions.explain: Health Cloud reshapes the standard model around Patients and Households, reflecting that many healthcare relationships involve a family unit, not just one isolated individual.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend modeling communication consent as its own record per patient per channel, rather than a single checkbox field?
options: Because Salesforce does not allow more than one checkbox field per object
Because checkbox fields cannot be referenced by a Flow
Because HIPAA specifically bans the use of checkbox fields
Because a single overwritten checkbox leaves no audit trail of what the patient agreed to and when, and can't represent different preferences across different channels
questions.explain: The requirement is per-channel, changeable, and auditable — a single checkbox field can't hold all three properties at once, which is why consent needs its own record with history.

questions.q: In this scenario, what is the key distinction between what Shield Platform Encryption protects and what the sharing model protects?
options: Encryption protects data from exposure outside the application (backups, exports, misconfigured integrations); the sharing model restricts which authorized users inside the application can see a given record
They protect the exact same risk, so only one is actually needed
Sharing rules replace the need for encryption entirely in a HIPAA context
Encryption only matters for financial data, not PHI
questions.explain: Treating encryption and sharing as solving two different problems — exposure outside the app versus visibility inside it — is exactly the distinction a HIPAA-focused design question is testing.

questions.q: What is step-up authentication, as used for viewing lab results or messaging a provider in this scenario?
options: A one-time password required only the very first time a patient ever logs in
An additional identity check triggered specifically at a higher-risk action, beyond whatever authentication happened at login
A requirement that patients change their password every 30 days
A feature that locks the account permanently after any failed login attempt
questions.explain: Step-up authentication adds a narrower, action-specific identity check for the small number of higher-risk actions, rather than treating the initial login as sufficient for everything in the session.

questions.q: Why does the design keep the EHR as the system of record for clinical data instead of letting Salesforce store the authoritative diagnosis history?
options: Because Salesforce technically cannot store medical data under any circumstances
Because HIPAA requires all clinical data to be stored outside of any CRM
Because the EHR vendor contractually forbids any integration with Salesforce

Because duplicating the authoritative clinical record in Salesforce risks creating a second, out-of-sync version of the truth, when Salesforce's actual job here is the engagement layer, not the system of record
questions.explain: The architectural reason is about avoiding a shadow, drifting copy of the authoritative record — not a technical or contractual prohibition.
